slides.body: Powertrain solutions

slides.title: Solutions Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
SolutionsHybrid vehicles
○ Mild Hybrid Electric Vehicle (MHEV): Vehicle
driven by a combustion engine powered by a
compact electric motor. It can have the electric
motor in different positions.
○ Full Hybrid Electric Vehicle (FHEV): It has both
combustion and electric engines. At low speeds and
short distances, a fully electric propulsion is
possible.
○ Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV): It
reaches higher speeds and longer distances unlike
the Full Hybrid. They can only be charged from
external points and can have a larger battery pack
than the FHEV, because the size is not limited to
the stored kinetic energy.

slides.title: P0, P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
Hybrid vehicles uses an internal combustion
engine (ICE) and at least one electric motor
(eMotor or EM).
In hybrid electric vehicles we can find many
abbreviations as P0, P1, P2, P3, P4 and P5.
Each abbreviation depends on the position of the
electric motor in the hybrid powertrain.
In some way, the number identifies the distance
between the electric motor and the wheels, which
decreases from P0 to P5.

slides.title: P0 and P1 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
P0 and P1Hybrid vehicles
○ P0 configuration: The EM can be mounted in
place of the alternator and then connected to the
engine with a belt. These are Belt-driven Starter
Generators (BSG) which also act as a starter motor
and generator.
○ P1 configuration: The EM is inserted on the motor
shaft. It runs at the same speed as the crankshaft
and requires some more modifications.

slides.title: P0 and P1 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
○ Audi System (P0 configuration)
1) DC-DC converter
2) 12V battery
3) 48V battery
4) Integrated BSG
5) ICE
P0 and P1Hybrid vehicles

slides.title: P2 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
○ P2 configuration: The electric motor is placed between the engine and the transmission, directly on the
shaft or through a gearbox. The engine insertion system implies a clutch that disconnects the ICE. So it
is possible to drive in full electric by the opening of the clutch.
P2Hybrid vehicles

slides.title: P2 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
○ Porsche Panamera System (P2 configuration)
1) ICE
2) EM
3) ZF Transmission
4) Battery pack
P2Hybrid vehicles

slides.title: P2.5 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
○ P2.5 configuration: This configuration is possible only with a Dual Clutch Transmission. The electric
motor is placed inside the transmission, on one of the two concentric transmission shafts, so that one
shaft (the one of the odd gears) is completely driven by the ICE, while the other one (even gears) is
driven also by the electric machine. Electric creaping/drive is possible by moving just the even gear shaft,
but also combined combustion and electric power mode is possible.
P2.5Hybrid vehicles

slides.title: P3 and P4 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
○ P3 configuration: This configuration moves the
engine “downstream” of the gearbox. In this way,
losses are minimized, since the electric motor only
drives the final part of the transmission.
○ P4 configuration: The EM acts exclusively on the
axis not connected to the ICE. In this way it is
possible to have an all-wheel drive without
mechanical connection with the thermal engine.
Even the pure electric mode is easily obtainable, by
disconnecting the main transmission.
P3 and P4Hybrid vehicles

slides.title: P3 and P4 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
○ Toyota Prius IV (P4 configuration)
1) ICE
2) Battery pack
3) Induction EM
4) Inverter
P3 and P4Hybrid vehicles

slides.title: P5 Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
○ P5 configuration: For hybrid and full electric vehicles there is the acronym P5 which indicates the
motors in the wheels, a solution that eliminates the "distance". This abbreviation, unlike those P0, P1, P2,
P3 and P4, has a still limited application in production cars.
P5Hybrid vehicles

slides.title: P1+P2 and P1+P4 configurations Hybrid vehicles
slides.body:
○ P1 + P2 and P1 + P4 configurations: P2 to P4 configurations as said have the
electric motors placed after the clutch, connected to the driveline side, and that, can
improve overall electrical performances; one of the most useful functionality of recent
ICE vehicles is inhibited: S&S. To avoid this, another electric motor (a P1) can be
added to the engine side enabling S&S functionality and enlarging hybrid strategies n
terms of load shift, torque assist, regeneration etc... On the other hand, complexity
and costs increase exponentially due to the addition of another motor that should work
together all the other components. This configuration essentially combines both
benefits and disadvantages of P1, P2 and P4s.
P1+P2 and P1+P4 configurationsHybrid vehicles

slides.title: BEV Full electric vehicles
slides.body:
BEVFull electric vehicles
○ Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV): The powertrain of an EV powered by battery is the simplest one among
all vehicles. It must include an Onboard Battery Charger (OBC) and there are several solutions for its
configuration.

slides.title: FCEV Full electric vehicles
slides.body:
FCEVFull electric vehicles
○ Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle (FCEV): The electrical powertrain is the same as for BEV, the difference
comes from the energy source (fuel cell). In the figure there is the system used by Toyota Mirai.

slides.title: Hybrid Advantages and disadvantages
Hybrid vs Electric Advantages and disadvantages
slides.body:
The real question that most people are asking now is: Is electric or hybrid more convenient?
Electric cars are made up of an electric powertrain that ensures zero emissions, therefore they allow
you to move without polluting. Despite this, some negative aspects must be considered: the costs of a
completely electric reality are still very high, the limitation linked to autonomy and the need to plan
each journey based on the battery recharge needs.
The hybrid car is more suitable for those who have to travel many kilometers a year, in this way it is
possible to benefit from greater autonomy, while still reducing carbon dioxide emissions and average
consumption.
The hybrid is also the best solution for those who do not have re-charging infrastructures, in fact in the
absence of electric stations it is still possible to circulate in petrol mode.
Hybrid vehicles can also be advantageous for those who need more flexibility, for example for driving
both on the motorway and in the city. In this case it is possible to take advantage of the performance of
the internal combustion engine in the extra-urban context, while in the urban one with the plug-in hybrid
or full hybrid it is possible to travel with zero emissions in the city up to 40-60 km.
Hybrid vs ElectricAdvantages and disadvantages

slides.title: Hybrid vs LPG Advantages and disadvantages
slides.body:
Is it better hybrid car or LPG?
Quite a doubt, however, concerns the convenience of a
hybrid car compared to a LPG car. In fact, gas is a fuel with
an advantageous price, as it costs about half compared to
petrol. However, it is also more polluting, in addition to the
costs for the system, including the mandatory review of the
cylinder and replacement after 10 years.
Naturally there is no single answer, in any case a LPG
vehicle is convenient for those who travel many kilometers in
the city, or as an alternative to diesel cars. Hybrid cars are
suitable for those who want a more versatile car that
generally lasts longer, moreover it is a more ecological
mobility option than LPG and versatile for those who travel
often even in the extra-urban context.
Hybrid vs LPGAdvantages and disadvantages

slides.title: Hybrid on highway Advantages and disadvantages
slides.body:
Is a hybrid car worth it on the highway?
The efficiency of hybrid cars is reduced on the highway, in fact in these situations the electric motor is
not very effective, as the petrol or diesel one is mainly used. The absence of electric powertrain
support does not allow to maintain low consumption and emissions, with worse performance than
driving in the city and on extra-urban roads.
For those who drive mainly on the motorway, the most suitable option is not the hybrid, but it is better
to opt for pure electric or highly efficient diesel cars. The former also allow you to travel on the
motorway network without polluting, despite the fact that the infrastructure is not yet widespread, the
latter ensure good consumption and low emissions thanks to the latest generation diesel engines
which allow you to save fuel on the motorway
Hybrid on highwayAdvantages and disadvantages
